I have farmed these 8 mu for 25 years. I never went to school, but I know this land by touching it. I watch what my neighbors do, and I remember what went wrong last year.

For wheat, I rotary till before sowing in October. Last year I used one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and I will do the same — that is about 8 kg phosphorus and 7 kg potassium per mu right there. Then at green-up I spread 15 kg urea, and at jointing another 20 kg urea. All together that is about 26 kg nitrogen per mu. My cousin tried to save money on fertilizer three years ago and his wheat turned yellow and thin — the yield was terrible. I would rather spend the extra 200 yuan than risk that. I irrigate three times from my well: wintering water, jointing water, and grain filling water. The electricity bill hurts, but dry wheat is worse. I spray twice — once for weeds after sowing, and once for aphids when the weather warms up. I use the improved wheat seed from the shop, the same kind my neighbor Lao Wang used last year. If the frost does not kill it, I expect 550 kg per mu.

For maize, right after I cut the wheat in June, I direct seed hybrid corn into the stubble without ploughing. No time to till, and last year the no-tillage maize yielded the same — why pay for extra diesel? I put about 40 kg compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then at big trumpet stage I spread 35 kg urea per mu. That comes to about 22 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once when the leaves start rolling in July heat, and once at grain filling in August. Two pesticide sprays — one for weeds, one for corn borer. Everyone in the village sprays for corn borer, so I do too. I expect 600 kg per mu. 

A bag of compound fertilizer is 150 yuan, urea is over 100 yuan now. For 8 mu it is a big pile of money. But I have six mouths to feed, and two of my family send some money back from factory work — that helps me buy the inputs. I never cut fertilizer to save money. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost you accept.
